claims.statement: Open-Inspect is a single-tenant background coding agent system: all users share one GitHub App installation scope and can access any repository the App can reach, and the system performs no per-user repository access validation before creating a session. GitHub users' OAuth tokens are used only for PR creation (bot fallback for non-GitHub sign-ins), while clone/fetch/push uses a shared App installation token.

The system is organized as three tiers connected by WebSockets: the web client (Next.js), the Cloudflare control plane (Durable Objects + D1), and the sandbox data plane (Modal, Python), plus three Hono bot workers (slack-bot, github-bot, linear-bot); the canonical flow is user prompt → client → control plane session DO (WebSocket) → sandbox → streaming events back through the same WebSocket chain.

The TypeScript packages form a single dependency root: @open-inspect/shared is imported by control-plane, web, slack-bot, github-bot, and linear-bot, and must be built first whenever shared types change; the root build and typecheck scripts enforce this ordering by building the shared package before the workspaces.

Durations carry their unit in the identifier: milliseconds in TypeScript with a _MS suffix (e.g. EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS, INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS) and seconds in Python with a _seconds suffix (e.g. DEFAULT_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 7200); bare timeout names are prohibited, and each default value is defined exactly once as a named constant.

Session state is split by design: the DO-embedded SQLite is the session's authoritative aggregate (session, participants, messages, events, artifacts, sandbox rows, WebSocket client mappings), while the global D1 database holds the listing/index mirror and config (session index, repo metadata, environments, secrets, automations, image builds, skills, users, pull-request records).

Each session id maps 1:1 to a SessionDO Durable Object (env.SESSION.idFromName(sessionId)); SessionDO is a thin platform adapter that on first activation applies the SQLite schema and eagerly builds the whole session runtime via createSessionRuntime (src/session/components.ts), which constructs every repository, service, and handler including the provider and SCM factories that throw on misconfigured deployments.

The control-plane Worker has three platform entrypoints: fetch handles the HTTP API plus WebSocket upgrades (a WebSocket upgrade on /sessions/:id/ws is validated against the D1 session index then forwarded to the SessionDO, everything else goes through the composable router); scheduled runs the per-minute automation/scheduler tick, the image-build scheduler cron, and the abandoned-draft sweep; queue consumes image-build finalization and GitHub Autofix batches.

The control plane routes requests through a composable router (src/router.ts) with per-route authentication policies: public routes, Better Auth user sessions, sig1 service-to-service signatures, and sandbox tokens that stay router-verified because they need the session id from the path and a DO round-trip; route handlers must use the instrumented ctx.db handle rather than the raw env.DB binding (ESLint-enforced under src/routes and src/webhooks).

Sandbox lifecycle is orchestrated by SandboxLifecycleManager (src/sandbox/lifecycle/manager.ts), which uses pure decision functions from decisions.ts for policy (spawn, inactivity timeout, heartbeat health, connecting timeout, warm decision, circuit breaker) and executes side effects through injected dependencies; it owns the in-memory isSpawningSandbox flag to prevent concurrent spawns.

Sandbox providers plug in behind the SandboxProvider interface (src/sandbox/provider.ts) with declared capabilities (snapshot/restore, persistent resume, explicit stop, timeout enforcement); supported backends are Modal, Daytona, E2B, OpenComputer, and Vercel Sandboxes, with Modal/Vercel/OpenComputer supporting prebuilt-image builds and snapshot restore while Daytona and E2B use persistent sandbox stop/start.

Sandbox lifecycle state is authoritative across WebSocket reconnects: losing the sandbox WebSocket does not stop the sandbox — the bridge reconnects while the control plane schedules a heartbeat check; explicit lifecycle paths (inactivity, stale heartbeat) persist stopped/stale status before closing the connection, which prevents reconnection.

The in-sandbox Python runtime (packages/sandbox-runtime) is composed by entrypoint.py: RuntimeConfig.from_env feeds a SandboxSupervisor that manages repository boot (clone/sync via RepositorySynchronizer, .openinspect/setup.sh and .openinspect/start.sh hooks with default timeouts 300s/120s), the OpenCode server, the agent bridge process (maintains the WebSocket back to the control plane), code-server, web terminal, browser desktop, and managed-skills materialization into the OpenCode global config.

Repo owners may be nested namespaces (GitLab subgroups like group/subgroup) — only repo_name is a single path segment, derived from checkout directories under /workspace; the sandbox validates this via is_safe_repo_owner / _require_safe in repo_config.py, and AGENTS.md instructs TypeScript code to split on the last '/' and encode the owner as one API route segment.

Session creation writes D1 before the DO is initialized, and failures must be caught before any sandbox spawn; provider and SCM factory construction is eager and throws on misconfigured deployments so a misconfiguration fails every session request at initialization rather than running degraded.

Automations and inbound webhooks are handled by the control plane with a shared trigger framework in @open-inspect/shared/triggers (types, condition registry, github/sentry/slack/webhook event types), the D1-backed scheduler (src/scheduler/scheduler.ts), workflow automation state, and control-plane webhook routes (src/webhooks/: automation-event, github, sentry, slack) authenticated with sig1 service-to-service signatures.

Three Hono bot workers sit on the client edge: slack-bot (Slack events/signature verification, target classifier, thread continuity, completion delivery via Cloudflare Queue), github-bot (GitHub webhook signature verification, KV delivery dedupe with 7-day TTL, auto-review and @mention triggers, autofix ingress), and linear-bot (Linear AgentSessionEvent webhooks to create/continue sessions) — each signs its control-plane requests with the sig1 service signature.

The web client (packages/web) is a Next.js app whose server-side API routes (src/app/api/**) forward to the control plane with the user's Better Auth session (controlPlaneUserFetch), explicitly picking allowed fields from client bodies because identity and SCM provenance derive from authenticated control-plane state; middleware applies correlation headers (x-trace-id, x-request-id) to /api/* requests.

Structured logging is shared across services via @open-inspect/shared/logger (flat JSON lines, logger-owned keys level/component/msg/ts/service) with a CorrelationContext of trace_id (x-trace-id), request_id (x-request-id), session_id, and sandbox_id propagating through HTTP headers, and scripts/cf-logs.ts provides log querying across worker logs.

D1 migrations live under terraform/d1/migrations/ as numbered SQL files and are applied by Terraform to production and automatically by the control-plane integration test pool (applyD1Migrations with the real migration directory); the pool's per-file shared D1 instance requires cleanD1Tables() cleanup in beforeEach/afterEach to avoid cross-test pollution.

Testing is split by ecosystem: TypeScript packages use Vitest (control-plane unit tests co-located as src/**/*.test.ts in the Node environment, integration tests in test/integration/**/*.test.ts running inside a real workerd runtime via @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers with real D1 bindings, Durable Objects, queues, and WebSockets); Python packages use pytest with pytest-asyncio (modal-infra tests/test_*.py, sandbox-runtime tests); module-boundary and lint-complexity checks run as structural gates, and CI runs lint, typecheck, and tests on every push and PR.

Deployment is full-stack Terraform under terraform/environments/production with modules per platform (cloudflare-worker, vercel-project, modal-app, daytona-infra, e2b-infra, opencomputer-infra, vercel-sandbox-infra, cloudflare-kv), web_platform choosing Vercel vs Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext, and a Terraform GitHub Actions workflow auto-deploying on pushes to main; known gotchas include PKCS#8 GitHub App keys, two-phase Durable Object binding deploy, and no checked-in wrangler.toml.

Managed skills are a shared subsystem: skills are assigned globally or to repositories/environments, personal skill profiles exist, revisions are content-addressed (hashSessionSkillManifest with a resolver version), git import/reimport materializes skill files, each session resolves and pins an immutable manifest (SessionSkillManifestInput with manifestSha256) before sandbox creation, and the sandbox-side ManagedSkillsMaterializer writes skills into the OpenCode global config directory.

The model catalog is centralized in @open-inspect/shared/models (MODEL_CATALOG with per-model reasoning-effort configs, default model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6), and subscription-backed provider accounts (ChatGPT, SuperGrok) are managed by the control plane via device authorization flows with provider-auth snapshots pinned per session and automation.

Sessions have exactly four mutually exclusive target modes (single repository, ordered multi-repo list up to MAX_TARGET_REPOSITORIES=10, a saved environment, or no repository) enforced by hasExclusiveSessionTarget, the first repository is the primary driving defaults (integration settings, secret collision precedence, scalar mirror columns), and session targets can also be resolved through environment routing (repo metadata defaultEnvironmentId for GitHub-bot, Slack routing rules/channel associations, Linear team/project mappings).

Pre-built images are built per repo or per environment: the image-build subsystem (src/image-builds/) plans builds from fingerprints, triggers provider build sandboxes with callback authentication, finalizes via a Cloudflare Queue consumer, and runs a maintenance reaper with rebuild policy; sandbox boot modes (fresh, repo_image, snapshot_restore, build) select whether setup.sh runs.

PRs are per-repository with user-vs-bot attribution: user OAuth tokens create PRs for GitHub sign-ins (bot fallback otherwise), a session can hold one open PR per head branch (re-calling the endpoint force-pushes and reuses the PR with updated: true), head branches default to the generated open-inspect/<session> branch, and webhook-driven pull-request-lifecycle tracking refreshes PR state; GitHub autofix ingests review feedback into new fix sessions.

Session diffs capture changes via a git-backed protocol between the sandbox runtime and control plane: an immutable base commit is compared, bounded patch bundles (versioned schema mirrored between Python and shared TS) are uploaded to the session-diff store with retry/failure handling, and the web UI consumes them for display.

Child sessions let agents spawn parallel sub-tasks: the spawn-child tool (sandbox) and spawn-child route (control plane) create child sessions in their own sandboxes with depth caps, the D1 child_admission_leases store atomically enforces maxConcurrentChildSessions (429 on exhaustion), send-child-prompt queues follow-up instructions into direct children, and get-child-status/cancel-child coordinate them.

Secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and scoped globally, per-repository, or per-environment; environment-launched sessions receive global + environment secrets (repository secrets do not flow in), and each session resolves its final environment-var set (user-env-resolver) for sandbox injection.
